chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sayyari from Abu Suleiman al-Khawwas from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn from Sadir al-Sayrafi who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and upon me was a white sandal. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadir! What is this sandal? Did you wear it knowingly?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you!' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who enters the market intending a white sandal, will not wear it out until he acquires wealth from where he does not expect.' Abu Nu'aym said, 'Sadir informed me that he did not wear out that sandal until he acquired one hundred dinars from where he did not expect.'

key_terms.مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ: from where he does not expect

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of wearing or buying a white sandal according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the specific intention (*niyyah*) behind a mundane purchase to divine providence (*rizq*), illustrating the Shia concept that conscious devotion in daily acts invites unexpected sustenance. The narrative highlights the spiritual significance of intentionality, where the act of seeking a white sandal becomes a vessel for receiving wealth from unforeseen sources, a theme resonant with the promise of 'sufficient provision' in the Quran.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Sayyari, from Abu Suleyman Al Khawwas, from Al Fazl Bin Dukeyn, from Sadeyr Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and upon me were white sandals. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Sadeyr! What is this sandal? Did you wear this knowingly?’ I said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who enters the market intending the white shoes, would not renew it (buy another new pair) until he attains wealth from where he did not expect’. Abu Nuaym said, ‘Sadeyr (the narrator) informed me that he did not renew that sandal until he had attained one hundred Dinars from where he did not expect’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Sayyariy from abu Sulayman al-Khawwas from al-Fadl ibn Dukin from Sadir al-Sayrafiy who has said the following:

“I once visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and I was wearing a white shoe. He (the Imam) asked, ‘O Sadir, are you wearing this shoe intentionally?’ I replied, ‘No, by Allah, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Whoever goes to the market place to buy a white shoe, it will not become old before he earns an asset from a source that he never expected to earn.’ Abu al-Nu’aym has narrated to me that Sadir said, ‘That shoe did not become old until I earned one hundred dinar from an unexpected source.’”
